memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons and then present them as a wave offering to the Lord. In this way you are to set the Levites apart from the other Israelites, and the Levites will be mine. After you have purified the Levites and presented them as a wave offering, they are to come to do their work at the tent of meeting." - Num 8:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God says it plainly: "the Levites will be mine." After being cleansed and offered, they belonged to God in a special way. They were set apart from the rest — not because they were better, but because God had claimed them for Himself.

To belong to God is the greatest privilege a person can have. The Levites were the Lord's own, dedicated to His service, marked out as His. There is deep security and identity in belonging to God. We are not adrift, owned by no one, living for nothing. We belong to Him.

Notice the order once more: cleansed, offered, then "they are to come to do their work." Belonging comes before working. First they were made God's; then they served. Our service always flows out of our belonging, never the other way around. We do not work in order to belong to God; we belong to God, and so we work.

This is wonderfully true for every believer. Through Christ, we are able to say, "I am not my own; I was bought at a price" (1 Cor 6:19-20). We belong to the Lord — in life and in death, "we belong to the Lord" (Rom 14:8).

Rest today in the security of belonging to God. You are His — cleansed, claimed, and called. Let your service flow gladly out of that settled truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you find security in belonging to God?
- Does your service flow out of belonging, or do you serve to earn belonging?
- What does it mean to say "I am not my own"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I belong to You — cleansed, claimed, and called as Your own. Let my service flow gladly out of the security of being Yours. Amen.
